description: Local-first multimodal synthetic-content detection dashboard for text, audio, image, and video, with explainability views.
constraints: MVP must run locally without heavyweight production models.
Use deterministic mock or heuristic detectors first, with clear interfaces for later model replacement.
Azure deployment is out of scope for this phase.

questions.question: Which language should the detection API use?

options.label: Python
options.description: Best fit for FastAPI, media processing, and later ML model integration.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Good for a Node.js API, but less aligned with the planned ML ecosystem.

questions.rationale: The requested backend is FastAPI and the project may later integrate Python ML tooling.

questions.question: Which backend framework and API shape should the MVP use?

options.label: FastAPI REST API
options.description: Async, typed endpoints for upload, detection, health, and explanation results.

questions.question: Describe the backend MVP features and the boundary between heuristic/mock detection and production models.
questions.recommendedChoice: Implement upload and analysis endpoints for text, audio, image, and video; return deterministic heuristic/mock scores with modality-specific evidence; expose health and version endpoints; keep detector interfaces replaceable for production models.
questions.answer: Implement upload and analysis endpoints for text, audio, image, and video; return deterministic heuristic/mock scores with modality-specific evidence; expose health and version endpoints; keep detector interfaces replaceable for production models.
questions.rationale: This matches the local-first MVP constraint and avoids requiring heavyweight models.

questions.question: Which language should the dashboard use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Typed component UI with a clear API contract and responsive dashboard interactions.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Simpler setup with less static type checking.

questions.rationale: The request allows React or Streamlit; React is recommended for a richer dashboard experience.

questions.question: Which UI framework should the MVP use?

options.label: React + Vite
options.description: Responsive dashboard with reusable modality panels and interactive explainability views.

options.label: Streamlit
options.description: Fastest Python-first prototype with simpler UI composition and less frontend separation.

questions.rationale: React best supports the requested dashboard and XAI visualizations while Streamlit remains a viable rapid prototype.

questions.question: Describe the dashboard experience and the XAI evidence each modality should show.
questions.recommendedChoice: Single-page local dashboard with drag-and-drop or text input, modality selector, analysis status, risk score and confidence, history for the current session, and evidence views: text highlights, audio spectrogram placeholder, image/video heatmap placeholder, plus an explicit label that MVP evidence is heuristic/mock until production models are integrated.
questions.answer: Single-page local dashboard with drag-and-drop or text input, modality selector, analysis status, risk score and confidence, history for the current session, and evidence views: text highlights, audio spectrogram placeholder, image/video heatmap placeholder, plus an explicit label that MVP evidence is heuristic/mock until production models are integrated.
questions.rationale: This covers the DeepGuard concept while keeping the first implementation lightweight and honest about model maturity.

sharedQuestions.question: Which data stores are required for the MVP?

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Keep uploads and analysis history in memory or temporary files for the local session.

options.label: SQLite
options.description: Persist local analysis metadata and session history without external services.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Persist uploaded media or analysis artifacts as objects.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Use a relational database for multi-user or production-scale metadata.

sharedQuestions.rationale: SQLite provides local persistence for analysis metadata and current-session history without introducing an external service.

sharedQuestions.question: Should users sign in to access application API features in the MVP?

options.label: Yes
options.description: Require sign-in before using the API and dashboard.

sharedQuestions.rationale: Authentication is not needed to validate the local MVP workflow.
